title: The case I needed.
text:
I work in a private gymnastics gym as a coach. Everything I own and bring to the gym gets thrown, dropped, beaten, spilled upon, chalked up and just generally abused by at least one of one hundred kids almost daily.

So when I got my iPhone I knew I needed something to protect it before I was looking to pay a huge repair bill.

Enter this case.

First off the shipping took longer than I expected. Most items I order from Amazon get to my house in ~2 days as there is an amazon distribution center less than three hours from my house. This took a full week. I'm not complaining but I thought it was odd.
Once I received the case I pulled it out of its packaging. I expected the case to weigh more than it did. I thought I would be adding serious weight to my phone. Something I was okay with. But it was surprisingly lightweight, I was slightly disappointed. I follow the directions and put the case on and went about my day.
It slid in and out of my pocket with ease, something I was only marginally concerned about. My number one goal for the case was protection, ease of use is secondary, so the rubber clinging to my fabric wasn't really a concern, and as it turns out a non-issue. It just doesn't happen.
Once I get to the gym, the kids see my phone. They say it looks like a bumble bee. Some like it, some dont. I think it looks supa dupa fly.
We have weights in the gym that we use for strength and conditioning and the kids were using them last night. I had sat my phone down on a mat and walked away to spot something. Its tough to keep things in your pocket and spot at the same time, so my phone is often left laying.
About half an hour after I left my phone I went back to get it and to my horror one of the kids had dropped a weight (45 lbs) on my phone. I'm glad they avoided dropping it on their toes, but really? My iPhone was the only good place to let it fall? On the right side of the screen there was a huge crease about two inches long and the hard plastic case's beveled edge is dented.
I immediately took off the case to see how much my week old iPhone was damaged.

Not. A. Scratch.

In the future I'm probably not going to leave my phone by the weights but knowing this happened gives me peace of mind.

I always read the bad reviews first so I'll try to cover some of the things negative I read.
Number 1. The oily screen issue. Not on mine. Not even a little. IDK if they changed their product or what but there's no residue between the plastic protector and the screen.
Number 2. The holster. My first issue with people complaining about it falling off of their belt is this; what kind of pretensions loser are you that you can't slide it in your pocket or purse? Personally I will never, never use the clip but for those that will (I'm currently rolling my eyes) if you turn the phone around so that the screen is facing your body it will fit quite snuggly. I snapped mine in and I was surprised at how much force I had to use to get it off the holster. It makes more sense to have the screen face you, as it adds a layer of protection against bumping into things.
Number 3. "It's chunky" I saw this a few times and it does add a bit of girth but I like it. I'm a large man and the phone fits my hand better now than it did without the case. I feel like I'm grabbing something, rather than feeling like I was reaching for something dainty like I did with the phone. It might not be your cup of tea but I like the feel. I mean I dont feel like I'm picking up a paperback novel but it is thicker.
Number 4. "It makes the screen less responsive" Less responsive than it already was? Nope. I simply have not noticed it, at all.
Number 5. "It hurts my fingers" One reviewer said that pressing the button and scraping the edges with their fingers made them sore. Seriously? If this product hurts your fingers you should probably at some point in the next month do some manual labor. I mean, you know, just to see what its like. That way you'll kind of know what your asking "the help" to do. Maybe you could get your butler to press the button for you, I dont know.

So thats my review of this case. I'm a big fan so far. It is heavy duty enough for my needs, it looks good, it feels good. $30 was totally worth it for the protection given.

text:
I loved this case at first and probably would have given it 5 stars off the bat, but since I've been using it now for a couple of months (January-May) it is showing a large amount of wear. I am very gentile with my belongings and treat them well--so when I spent $45+ on this case, you can bet that I treated both it and my new iPhone 4S like a newborn baby.

But even with my carefulness, I still found the edges of this case to be turning a dirty off-color. I tried wiping it off, even with a Mr. Clean magic eraser, and saw no improvement. From there it only got worse; the corners started peeling--first a clear layer and then the color. So now I have a dirty looking case with paint-chipped edges. It's rather sad looking because even the design on the back has turned to a brownish white.

Would I buy this again, maybe. But having the experience that I have had with my OtterBox now, I'm not sure I would be willing to pay this much for a case that will start to loose it's bright color and paint within a month (or so).

Oh, and did I mention that my phone was bumped lightly and fell a total of 5 inches in this case and the screen broke. Yeah, thank you OtterBox for protecting my phone. **Funny story: a day before it fell off my lap while in a meeting and landed on the hard tile floor OtterBox free and still worked without a scratch**

My overall opinion (summed-up, in short): I think that for the price this product should have kept it's appearance for a bit longer.

title: Poor service from AT&T (and worse from Comcast!)
text:
The product looks OK... That is the only positive thing that I can say about it. I followed the instructions provided and was not able to get it to activate. I moved it closer to a window and was able to get a satellite lock but that means it is in an inconvenient place in the lounge room.

The help desk at AT&T is hopeless. I have been told lies such as "this is an incoming call center only and we are not able to call you back", "these are all of the things that could be wrong with the device so I am going to ask you to return it to the store and get another one" and "we have been experiencing a technical difficulty with activation of microcells and there is no estimated time or date that this could be rectified". Each time AT&T provided a "solution" such as reboot, you are required to leave it sit for 24 hours to give it time to connect.

I spoke to a manager as they seemed to have another clue in the puzzle to get this thing to activate. We are not given a choice of internet as we live in a condo. AT&T suggested that Comcast might have a block or firewall that was preventing the microcell from connecting. Apparently this is very common she assured me yet no one below supervisor level knows about it!! So off I went to speak with Comcast....

Comcast is perhaps the only customer service that is worse than that with AT&T!! A 15 minute wait time and then the operator had no clue, showed no interest in understanding what I was trying to do. When he suggested that I call back to the comcast platinum line to ask them (for a tiny sum of $5.99) I asked to speak to the supervisor- no dice there as the supervisor was "busy"!! That is just stupid. I pressed this and so off he went to find a supervisor who was not busy. He came back on the line to say..... I don't know as my phone dropped out again.

I figured I'd try calling Comcast again and hope that I had a better represenative.. I seem to have lucked out by speaking with a customer support representative who had worked with Retravision and knew about the microcell. Comcast assured me that there was no block on the service so back I went to AT&T.

I was told that if there was no block on the service from Comcast then AT&T would need to put the request in a technical ticket. As I have had no success with people calling me back, I decided to run the gauntlet again with the AT&T help line. I had the information that the people in the morning required from me (router make and model) but once again the helpdesk operator had me run through yet another process. Unlike his co-workers, he actually called me back as promised but still no activation. He was able to process the technical assistance request and I can now expect a 5 - 8 day wait for them to contact me (or not if they think that it has been fixed).

All of this with a phone that would drop out after 3 and 1/2 minutes.

In short for all involved:

AT&T - you need to provide your staff with better instructions than has no clue what they are doing with the microcell. The help desk is simply a Q&A desk and although each of the operators were cordial, they did not follow through as they suggested.

If you have the option to choose an alternative to Comcast then do it.

On both - exhaust all avenues with the person that originally answers the phone. If they can't help you, ask for their supervisor and exhaust all avenues that they may have. When that fails, call back until you get a satisfactory answer.

Cisco - either you have not provided AT&T with a satisfactory description of how to install the microcell or you are selling the microcell and it doesn't work.

Amazon - the price on this website is $399. AT&T sell the product at their shop for $199.... AT&T actually reimbursed me the cost of the cell.

Update - still nothing from AT&T. still working on it 8 days later.

title: Not an easy install, but it does work
text:
This is not just a wifi extension you plug into the wall that syncs to your router. Its a lot more complicated in terms of installation. You get a full package here where your house basically becomes and antenna for your phone line. To set it up, you will need to wire cables from inside your house, to outside and onto the roof. All of the components are necessary to properly secure the antenna on the roof to prevent it from moving. You will need to troubleshoot the best direction to face the antenna for the strongest signal.

I live in an area where the signal dips because its in a valley of sorts, so the signal gets lost somewhere around me. So I needed to find the spot that works best. It was not perfect, but it was stronger than it was. Once you find the spot and you secure the antenna, which is connected to the "box" or meter, then you can place the brackets on the wall which will holster the meter. And you are pretty much done.

It comes with an inside antenna as well, which you can use to help pick up some of the signal within the house to give it more boost. When all is said and done, you have a lot of cable wire to contend with. Unless you are a professional, its probably gonna be hard to deal with. I am by no means a professional and I am not sure the best way to keep all this wire under control and out of the way. So this is my contention with this item. Its a good device and pretty much a professional kit in my opinion, and so I think its not a great do it yourself kind of home kit.

title: Fake ETL verification
text:
Edit 1/5/23: I just received a response from Intertek/ETL who stated that their verification stamp on this charger was not authorized. The INIU company and the company listed on the charger (Shenzhen Topstar Industry Co) are not registered in ETL/Intertek’s global directory. ETL stands for Electrical Testing Laboratories and is responsible for “assurance, testing, inspection, and certification services” across many industries. An ETL stamp is very similar to a UL stamp, seeing as they both require products to meet the same electrical safety standards If the INIU company is selling products with fake certifications, I cannot trust those products or that company and I will not be using this charger and will be reporting this to Amazon.

Original review:

I bought this 45w charger to use around the house as a dual iPad and phone charger, with the option of charging my 2015 MacBook Pro. Yes 45w will charge a MBP, at least of that age, and I have a MagSafe adapter that connects to a 100w usb-c to usb-c cord. Unfortunately, this charger does not charge the MBP, even though my other 45w charger will. That is unfortunate, because that means I will have to pull out that other charger for the MBP, and I keep that other charger in my electronics "go-bag" for travel. One thing to note is that it DOES charge my girlfriends 2020 M1 MacBook Air, which requires less output in general to charge.

The other use case I bought this for if the the ability to charge my iPhone 13 Pro Max and my iPad Pro at the same time, and I'm happy to report that it works well for that. Charging is not the fastest on the iPad, but iPhone seems to charge normally.

The direction that the "45w" and "INIU" brand label are printed on this device seem upside down. When it is plugged in with the plugs on the top (which seems to be the standard way of plugging chargers into plugs) the text is upside down, so the high output port is on the bottom. Looking at the product photos, there is even an image of the prongs being on the top, with the text right-side-up, giving access to the top outlet in the photo. Probably just sloppy photoshop, but kind of annoying having to look through photos to figure out the high output vs low output ports since the "top port" is the 45w max port...top is subjective to how the charger is plugged in.

I just emailed ETL/Intertek to get verification of the ETL certification. I never trust Amazon sellers that are not name brand, and it's best to be careful since using products like this could void your home insurance or rental insurance if they cause a fire and are not actually ETL certified. I will edit my review once I get verification from ETL/Intertek.

title: Way too stiff - definitely an overkill and a mild annoyance
text:
First of all, it gets the job done, thus 3 stars.
Bought in July 2023

The biggest downside is the insane stiffness of the neck. It could have very well hold a 2 kg (4-5 lb) item instead of modern cellphone. It needs a lot of force required to adjust its position. The clamp that attaches to the furniture cannot get a grip that strong, so when you try to adjust the position with one hand you would often shift the clamp itself rather change the shape of gooseneck, so it is better to adjust with 2 hands. Base clamp is still good enough, no issues. Cellphone clamp is very light, and won't be able to hold a 2kg item though. It also gets the job done though, perfectly enough for modern smartphone, but you can't fit a tablet into if if you are curious.
Also, another praise for the cellphone clamp - very easy to put your phone in and take it out (compared to other designs).

One surprising downside of the insane stiffness of the neck is oscillation (vibration) that whenever you touch your phone screen you displace it slightly and your phone dangles back and forth a little bit, and those vibrations are annoying and they don't dissipate fast enough, so whenever I have to turn the page of the book I read, I will have to hold the phone with more than just my finger to let those vibrations dissipate into my hand. This will not be a problem if you plan to mostly watch videos, or if you use an auto-scroll feature for your reading. I think this will also lead for this gooseneck to be unsuited to be used in a vehicle (vibration from the vehicle will not dissipate fast).

Also, the neck happened to be shorter than I think it will be, but that is just my misperception.

Will be good to use for watching videos (no manual scrolling) and only in a place where you wouldn't want to adjust if frequently. Phone clamp holds phone great and is very easy to put the phone in and take it out.

text:
Excellent charger. Charges my S21 Ultra 5G at its fastest "super fast charging" speed. Listen I am generation Y. Born in the 80's when tech like cell phones and computers were just beginning to make their way into consumer hands. I say that to say this. I remember the day when you went to the store and you simply bought a charger that worked with your particular phone. Those days are no more. When you are looking to buy a charger these days you are not only looking for one that works with your particular phone but you are looking at its wattage and built in technology to determine the speed at which it will charge your phone.

Manufacture chargers are expensive, and for a while it was the only choice for a charger that could charge these modern cell phones at the 45 watt super fast speed. I guess those days are no more. This charger no only charges my phone at its fastest speed but it doesnt get hot while doing it. The power brick feel quality made and the prongs on the plug make a solid connection with the wall outlet. This is important because generic products such as this can often have flimsy plugs. This one does not. The 6.6ft usb-c cable that comes with it is plenty long and a lot better than the 3.5ft cable you get with manufacture chargers. I will say that even with that I dont like the usb-c cable that comes with this charger. It feels cheaply made and the usb connection is so tight you have to kind of force it in all the way, and that just isnt good for the longevity of the phone you are charging or the charger. So I opted to toss the cable and just use a not as long, but much better-quality manufacture cable that I have.

Even though the cable itself feels cheap to me and I opted not to use it with the charger, I still give this product a top-rated review. The reason being is because at this point of half the cost of a manufacture charger you are still getting the same benefits and you could purchase a better quality usb-c cable to use with this charger and still come out cheaper than purchasing a manufacture charger. The power brick is quality made, works flawlessly without getting hot and charges modern phones at their fastest charging speed, all at half the price of a genuine manufacture charger. There is a slots for 3 cards and a pouch for some dollar bills. It is worth noting that when closed, the top of your cards will rest on your screen. All the cutouts on the bottom of the case line up perfectly with the headphone jack, charging port and speaker grill.

You can position this case to use a viewing stand for videos or movies. I use it in this position to display my calendar while at my desk in the office.

Overall this is a good little wallet case for a fair price. The case will offer protection if dropped. It slides in/out of my pant pocket with no issues. It has become my daily case and I enjoy using it.

title: Mixed feelings. One good install, one failed.
text:
I have mixed feelings about the product. I installed mine first and thought it went super well. I could barely tell the protector was on (foreshadowing). Then I did my wife's phone and was disappointed when I could just barely see the edges on hers. It still looked nice, but not nearly as seamless as mine had. I then looked back to my phone to discover, much to by chagrine, that it was not installed at all! When I tore off the final installation alignment tab on the screen protector (following their directions, of course), it had ripped the entire screen protector that I just painstakingly installed off of my phone with it! I then tried reinstalling it, just to see if it would work after crumpling it up with the disposable tab, but it was obviously too far gone. Second photo is my phone after doing this, and the first is my wife's phone, which installed just fine.

I watched the installation video and read the included, printed instructions as a refresher while installing. I'm really not sure how it went so wrong except that that final alignment tab (which is adhered to the entirety of the screen protector itself) was just too sticky and peeled off the screen protector with it.

I am thus giving an overall 2-star review because the company shouldn't design a product that gets torn off so easily with its disposable alignment tabs. It is a great idea to have them, though, because my wife's installed just fine and was really well aligned with the sides and the camera at the top.

I do think the fingerprint reader works great, though, since it even worked through the bubbles on mine after reapplying the protector. The scratch resistance rating may change, but I'm already seeing some damage just from installation, so I'm not holding my breath.

If the company reaches out to offer a replacement, I may increase my rating slightly if the next install goes well. For now, I'm just going to be extra careful until I find another solution.

UPDATE: I have reached out to the company twice now for their "warranty" that is supposed to cover failed installations. Both times, I have received no response. Downgrading from 2 stars to 1. Still seems to be a decent product, but I hate dealing with companies that have zero customer support.

title: Amazing case to turn your iPhone into an UNDERWATER CAMERA! Great for snorkelling!
text:
[[VIDEOID:4b3339f59de9c065d55f26bf6c32deb0]] VIDEO OF CASE USED ON IPHONE 5 IN MAUI, HAWAII. SNORKELLING OFF THE END OF KAMAOLE II BEACH.

Bought this when on a trip to Hawaii and kept being amazed by the snorkelling and wanted to capture it. I almost bought a GoPro Hero 2 (couldn't afford the 3) but I was worried about the blurriness that appears on the normal (non-flat) lens. Found this and thought I couldn't really lose for $10, though I was nervous about it working. I have a few key points that I hope help.

1. WORKS SUPERBLY TO TURN AN IPHONE 5 INTO AN UNDERWATER CAMERA
I used this no less that 25 times on our trip and together with my iphone it took some amazing videos. I've uploaded a sample video as well.

2. CASE and LANYARD ARE VERY STRONG
My 2 year old son used it underwater, he stuck his hand in the case and wore it as a glove, it was used in rough seas just dragging behind no doubt putting strain on the lanyard attachment and never came close to coming off. And still keeps water out after being roughed up that much.

3. YOU CAN USE THE IPHONE 5 SCREEN UNDERWATER
Yes you can use the touch screen underwater. You just need to make sure that there is no other part of the case touching the screen as it then won't respond. The way to do this is to expand the sides of the case to fill it with air when closing it shut. The casing then isn't close to the phone (it kind of 'floats' around inside, at least the iphone 5 does) and when you press on the image capture button through the case it is fine. I did find that when diving deeper, the pressure pushed the case closer to the screen, and I had to make sure the phone was right in the middle of the case so that the screen wasn't touching the case at its edges.

Those are the key things I wanted to note. I hope the review is useful. I don't often write reviews, but I was so pleasantly surprised by this that i wanted to! I've even uploaded a youtube copy of the video because I couldn't find any sample videos taken with this case when I was buying.

NOTE: The video on amazon seems to be a bit rubbish. I've uploaded it to Youtube... Just search Youtube for "snorkel hawaii frieq" and it's the top hit. You can view in 720p and it looks a billion times better.

title: Did a lot of research on what was the best portable weatherproof blue tooth speaker for the best price
text:
I bought this little speaker about 5 months ago. Did a lot of research on what was the best portable weatherproof blue tooth speaker for the best price, and I felt comfortable spending $30ish dollars on this one. It was a good purchase - the speaker works well and it is easy to use for someone who is a novice at bluetooth. A couple things worth mentioning and why I'm only giving it three stars -

******If the speaker is paired with a device, it will not unpair itself. Maybe this is bluetooth 101; it was news to me. In context - if my boyfriend pairs his phone with the speaker while he's home in the morning and forgets to manually unpair before he leaves for work, I cannot pair my phone with the speaker when I get home and it is essentially unusable until he manually unpairs it with his phone. I've tried turning the speaker on and off, and I've tried pushing the bluetooth button on the speaker to get it to pair with a different device. The speaker will show up on my device as available, but I'll be unable to actually connect to it because it's still paired with my boyfriend's phone. So, if you are using the speaker in a household with more than one person, it may be difficult to actually use it unless you are all sticklers about unpairing it with your device after use. Make sense at all?
**I'm weird and like to listen to podcasts while I shower and get ready, hence why I was looking for a weatherproof speaker. When paired with my iPhone, the speaker does not get loud enough to comfortably listen to podcasts while the shower or sink is running, even with both the volume on my phone and the volume on the speaker turned up all the way.
**Don't have a car stereo, so I tried to experiment with bringing the speaker in my car and listening to podcasts while I drive. Same thing - speaker is not loud enough to audibly catch all the words in the podcast. I should probably just buy a car stereo.
**Speaker is not loud enough to listen to podcasts if you are doing the dishes (i.e. running any water or banging any pots or dishes around)

TLDR: don't get this to use for podcasts. If your sole purpose for it is to listen to music, it gets pretty loud and has a good bang for its buck. Oddly enough we have no problems using it as a music source for outdoor BBQ's and get togethers, it's just not very great for listening to podcasts. For a $30 speaker to just listen to music - go for it, it's great.

title: I really expected to give this product 5 stars, but unfortunately I can give it only 3. See below...
text:
I bought this case to protect my new iPhone 12 mini. It really reminded me of the silicone case I had on my iPhone 4G a decade ago, and I really looked forward to receiving it. I specifically chose the OtterBox brand as I bought a few cases of this brand in the past for my previous phones and were mostly pleased with their built quality.

However, when it arrived I have found that this case is not a pure silicone/flexible mold all around, but instead it is built from 2 pieces that are glued together: a silicone/flexible piece that covers the top half of the phone from the sides which also covers the buttons, and a pure PLASTIC piece that covers the bottom half of the phone and the camera area, which is not flexible and could easily break if your phone accidently falls on a hard floor.

While the description says "it's made with 50% recycled plastic and raised edges that protect camera and screen", it does not indicate that half of the case is pure plastic while the other half is silicone/flexible. I thought that it's a mixture of silicone and plastic all around so this is somewhat misleading.

True, it has MagSafe which works perfectly at both holding the phone in MagSafe mounts and charging, which is reasonable to have a higher price tag than a simple case without this feature, but for a $49.95 price tag I expected an all-around silicone/flexible material which handles falls and bumps better. And since this case is made for both iPhone 12 mini and iPhone 13 mini which have different cameras alignment, the camera protection area is not very good in my opinion as the case does not protect around the lenses, it's just a big rectangular opening where the cameras are still somewhat exposed on the back to "pointy" surfaces/objects.

Bottom line, it's a good case and it works quite well with the MagSafe feature. But if you're like me and looking for an all-around silicone/flexible case then this is not the one.

text:
Bottom Line Up Front - This is the best zfold3 case hands down.

This is case 3 for me. All 3 are good cases, but the other 2 had minor flaws.

Tech21 hybrid case was really nice because it was compact but did not protect the spine. That's really bad tho because ANY damage to the spine voids the warranty. I got dead pixels along the fold and they would not cover it because there was a tiny tiny chip at the edge of the spine. Had to use my asurion coverage and drop a $250 deductible.

So I got the spigen tough armor. It was super bulky but this phone will never be small...so no big deal. Main knock on it is how high the raised edges are from the screen. It makes it very difficult to type using any of the keys on the very left side - mainly 1 and Q. You will be hitting 2 and W a lot which is more frustrating than it sounds. Other than that, the tough armor was great.

This one though.. it's more compact and it feels great in hand. Typing is easy, and the spine is protected. Plus when in tablet mode, the spine protection makes the phone a little easier to hold on to.

This one feels like the best of both worlds. If the tech21 had a baby with the tough armor you get the Slim Armor Pro.

text:
My girlfriend suggested Tech Armor privacy screens and I really liked the one she got which was also from Tech Armor. It was a 4-way one for 4S found here: http://www.amazon.com/Tech-Armor-Ultimate-Protector-Replacement/dp/B008THTTMQ. I loved hers so I was really excited; however, I was slight disappointed.

Comparing 4S version to 5:
Comparing hers against mine, mine looked like I was looking through a window screen and you could see the cross hatches that help create the privacy. Her privacy screen does not have this, it's a very smooth black overlay kind of like when you use Photoshop and just put a black layer over your photo and lighten the opacity. Finally (although take this with grain of salt) the privacy screen seemed to do better on hers as when I sit next to her, it's hard to read her screen yet on mine it is somewhat easier. Not sure if this has to do with the iPhone 5 being slightly larger or my brightness setting versus hers but it was something we noticed.

The Good:
+ The product works as intended, it does help keep others from seeing easily what is on my screen (though still can't be totally next to me such as on a crowded subway station or bus).
+ It fits nicely and is clean and the product comes with a little card to smooth out bubbles and cleaning cloth which I thought was exceptional because I didn't have any nice cloth to use to clean my iPhone besides maybe a cotton shirt.
+ Easy instructions and application of the screen to the phone.

The Bad:
+ Misalignment on the camera and speaker opening. The opening is large enough that the camera and speaker aren't obstructed but it just isn't centered.
+ Small edges near home button are a bit white possibly not stuck fully to iPhone.
+ Cross hatches make it look like I'm looking through a window screen (see comparison above for more detail)

Overall:
I still like the product. Not sure if I like having a privacy screen/screen protector on top though so I'm still debating whether to keep or not but for the functionality it works and sticks to the iPhone nicely and was easy to put on.

title: Produce enough power to charge my phone, not very durable
text:
Good power output, enough to charge my phone and Nexus 7 pad in reasonable time, however, I question how durable the device is in the long term.

The entire solar panel is divided into three semi ridged sections. Each section puts out about 600mA under full sun. Each of the panel is designed to put out about 6V under full sun, there is a small regulator in the USB connector to convert it down to 5V for the device.

After receiving the device, although it looks fine, under microscope, I can see two of the panel have half of the solar cell cracked. As a result, the two damaged panel puts out about 450mA under full sun. This led me to question how easily these panel can have cracked cells resulting in degrading output capacity.

Packing weight for the panel is about 600g, it is a bit too heavy to use for backpacking.

Tested under full noon sun, output taken before the regulator, the short circuit current is 1558mA.

title: I saw this was a lower price than many out there so figured it was worth the loss if I didn't like it. I was actually impressed
text:
I was hesitant to get a VR set and all I want to do is us it for 3D movies. I saw this was a lower price than many out there so figured it was worth the loss if I didn't like it. I was actually impressed with the initial tests I did with some 3D movies. I really like the fact that the earbuds are built into the unit and retract. It also came with lens cloth and extra bud covers of different sizes and a little bag for everything to fit.

The strap is fine, easily adjustable, but it gives me the sense that it's going to slip back over my head. Not really sure how it could be lowered, per se, but I would feel more comfortable with it if it went further down the back of my head. It hasn't fallen off it's just mainly a sensation thing with me. The only actual "ehhh" thing I have is that they could add more foam to the nose area. Light comes in from under the nose guard and it's extremely noticeable. Some people may find this annoying enough to ruin the use of it but it isn't that bad for me. Turn off the lights, kick your feet up and enjoy. But definitely some extra padding or something in that area to serve as a light block is recommended for any future versions of this.

Despite being super cheap I wouldn't recommend it for younger kids. I don't think it would fit their heads if they're smaller and the gap would probably be even more noticable for them. I'd roughly estimate maybe 11/12 and older it might fit better.

Unfortunately, the case seems less appealing on multiple fronts than the 4s version. The two halves do not lock together as well, so the case often comes apart unintentionally. The version I had for the 4s was lined with a felt-like covering which is not present on the 5. The new version's buttons are very stiff, so the volume and lock buttons do not work smoothly. This was not a problem in the previous generation of this case.

In general, I feel like I got a lower quality case this time around than I did the previous two times. It's not necessarily bad, it's just that when comparing it to the iPhone 4 case, it feels like a step backwards. I'll keep it for now, but I'll be keeping my eyes open for a better option.

title: It's your standard ipega controller
text:
I've been through many ipega controllers and they all have the same problem. When it comes to the build quality, it's a bit below average. There's a lot of rough edges which shouldn't be there on a plastic injection molded shell. That's nothing compared to the biggest issue of this controller. Like other ipega controller, these analog sticks are awful. They tend to "stick" on the x and y axis, making it very hard to pull off precise movement. A lot of reviewers will pull up a few games in emulation and call it good, but in actual use they leave a lot to desire. This is especially noticeable in FPS where you need precise aim. That's practically impossible with these analog sticks. They're passable for 3D platformer since most of these games have a lot of leeway in terms of movement. If you want to ignore the stick and just use the d-pad and ABXY for platformers, that's also a challenge. Since both analog sticks are prioritize, it makes using the d-pad very uncomfortable.

I forgot to mention the gimmick of this controller, the module right side. It's kinda like the Joy-cons, but it fails to justify the gimmick. You can swap out the right controls with a basic trigger-only setup, but I don't see this ever being useful. There are controllers made with this control scheme, but if you already have a full controller why would you ever want to limit yourself. The use of USB-C is just for show, this will not charge with your USB PD charger (might even break it if you try).

Overall, this is a hard pass from me. The build quality is mediocre, the analog sticks are awful, and the gimmick is pointless. This may be the only telescopic controller that will accommodate a tablet, but it's not worth it.

text:
We live in a black hole, which I don't get why we are in the cities and shouldn't have issues, but we do at our house, us and anyone that comes here.

So we looked around and tried to find options, and This one wasn't too bad compared to others. I didn't dig much farther than looking at their listings. Which maybe I should have. But here we are non the less.

Day two finally know where we are going to put it, got it up no issues. Ran the wires down and into our garage, set up the device and went great! Should be good to go.

Once I realized that and moved it farther away it seemed to work and do what I needed of it! So now, we are one more time moving it to a different room farther away from the box,

So if you have time to put this up and can deal with trouble shooting this will work. It just took us a bit of trouble shooting to figure it out.

The app that was on the instructions was no good. We actually got a follow up email from tech saying to contact if we had any issues, and that was helpful. Was able to get the correct app, signalsupervisor app. And when we were on the roof could see where it was bad signal and good signal.

title: Great product if...
text:
The Zagg screen protectors, including the new one I've purchased for my iPhone 5, are perfect at doing what they're advertised to do. They are better than an other protector on the market, and the are great product if ***you know how to install them correctly***.

The instructions included with the screen protector sound easy, but it is really more of an acquired technique, and with me...trial and error since my first Zagg screen protector several years ago.

If you purchase one and aren't sure if you can put it on perfectly, let someone else do it (they offer a service at Best Buy...but you must pay for it). If you want to do the install on your own, watch others on You Tube and make sure ***every*** piece of dust, fiber, smudge, etc is cleaned off of the screen. I always use an iPhone screen cleaner and two types of cloths to get everything off. Also, make sure and wash your hands and spray the included solution on your fingers because natural oils on your fingertips are your enemy.

To sum it up, it's the best screen protector out there, but if you install it...make sure there is not a spec of dust or smudge print and your fingers are clean or you will end up with bubbles or edges that peel off. Install it correctly and it will last for years.

title: Severe design flaws, otherwise comfortable
text:
It seems to be constructed well enough but it is designed very poorly. My biggest complaint is that the home button is nearly unusable when the phone is lying flat, such as on a desk. When you try to press the home button when the phone is lying on a desk it jumps up and down like an unbalanced seesaw. This could have easily been prevented by having a little nub on the back of the phone under the home button to prevent the seesaw action. The other problem is that the rubber comes up too far on the face at the bottom where the capacitive buttons are. It's much more difficult to press the menu and back buttons and you have to be pretty careful and contort your thumb to hit it and not touch the screen. Several times I've hit the screen because I didn't contort my thumb around enough to actuate only the back button. This may not be an issue if you're fingers are tiny, though.

On the positive side it is a solidly built case and feels good to hold. The volume and power buttons require the perfect amount of pressure and is much needed because they are so low on the phone they are far to easy to accidentally press without the case. The kickstand works adequately but seems a bit flimsy due to the weak spring and wobbly in a direction it should not wobble.

title: Absolutely wonderful case that keeps to a slim design yet feels very well protected and sturdy!
text:
When my father-in-law first introduced me to this case, for my old iPhone 5, I instantly fell in love with it. Previously, I was using an Otterbox Defender which made the whole thing too bulky. I wanted to have a case that felt sturdy, protective, yet keep to the slim design of the phone... and Spigen was the answer. Not only did I love the interchangeable back plates, I loved the way it felt in my hand. It wasn't slippery or too big, and most importantly, it felt protected.

I recently bought this for my work phone, which is an S5... and I'm still loving the Spigen line. I always compare other cases to this one. I've also upgraded to the S5 Active, from my iPhone 5. Unfortunately, Spigen doesn't make cases for the Active phones so I had to settle for another case.

Here are some other details that I'd like to point out:

1. The cutouts in the case, for the headphone jack, speakers, camera, are all perfect. I have no issues with any of the cutouts blocking plugs, or making things hard to get to... it is all perfectly sized, imo.

2. The volume and power buttons are superb. They feel very sturdy and aren't loose at all. My power button seems to be a little stiff but it's not a huge deal.

3. If you buy this case, you'll need to get a screen protector. It's a small detail but I kind of hoped that it would have been included. Still, not an issue at all.

Overall, I would highly, highly recommend Spigen to anyone looking for a case that keeps to the phone's slim design, yet feels sturdy and protected.

title: Great product, works well, worth the money
text:
I bought this about a month ago for use in my car. I’ve been very happy with it and it works very well. I mounted the HaloLock with the included vent mount. While the included mount is not superb quality (the mount itself allows for a very small bit of rotation), it certainly works well and I haven’t had a reason to want to replace it. Keep in mind that the product itself comes with a standard ball attachment system, so you can attach it to any mount you already have in your car. The product itself is simply amazing. I use it with my iPhone 12 and an Apple MagSafe case (the ones apple makes). With this setup, the phone sticks perfectly to the center of the charger. It’s still easy to pull the phone off the charger (when you’re getting out of the car for example), but it sticks great, even going over large bumps. In fact, the only incident I’ve had with the phone falling was when the entire charger fell off my vent because I mounted it loosely. You can also stick the phone in any rotation and it will stay in that rotation. However it is difficult to rotate the phone on the charger without rotating the charger as well (due to the mount allowing some extra movement). I usually just pull it off and stick it back on in the rotation I want. I have not had to worry about the phone falling off the charger. I drive a Prius in an area with very poor road quality, so I’d say that the magnets would work in pretty much any normal situation. I don’t know if I’d trust it on a motorcycle or something like that though. In terms of charging, it is not the fastest, but I have consistently had it charge my phone even while running maps and other navigation which is usually taxing on the battery. It is not as fast as plugging the phone in, but if you are in the car for more than 15 minutes you will probably get 15-30% battery back. Keep in mind I use an iPhone 12, this may vary for other devices.

Overall, the product is very good, it looks nice, and it is incredibly easy to use. I would highly recommend!

title: be sure to watch the instructional video
text:
All of the Spigen products that I've had in the past have been top notch. However, at first I thought that this Spigen Galaxy S9 Screen Protector NeoFlex [ Flexible Film x 2 ] [ Case Friendly ] 2 Pack for Samsung Galaxy S9 (2018) product was just OK. That's because I ruined the first one because I thought that I knew how to do it (my bad). All over the packaging, it suggests that you view the instructional video. WATCH IT! It doesn't have any verbal instructions, but does tell you how to put the protector on with minimal fuss/muss. As soon as I put it on, I still saw streaks and other specks. However, after not too long (no more than an hour), it seems that all of the blemishes went away. The steps in the instructional video certainly worked for me. It tells you when/how to use the liquid spray that is included in the package, the scraper, the cloth and (of course), the screen protector itself. I was surprised when one of its first steps was to use the spray on my hands. But that does make sense.

Here are the steps that I got from their instructional videoL
1) put phone in the case
2) turn phone longways
3) wipe off screen with cloth
4) use sticky tape to remove any remaining lint
5) spray your fingertips with spray and rub into your finters
6) while your hands are still wet, remove the protector from the paper. The spray the side that goes down on your phone. Roll around so that the liquid is even on the protector. Place on your phone. You will still be able to adjust it.
7) spray again and use scraper to adhere the protector to the screen. Go down the middle first and then go from the middle towards the outside.
8) wipe with the cloth and then remove the phone from the case. Then using the cloth, adhere the protector to the edges of your phone.

I hope that this helps but don't quote me! It is just my interpretation of the instructional video.

One final note - let it dry and if you have any remaining liquid or bumps, those should go away. At least it did for me.

Good luck!

title: Significantly Different Design Compared to Bodyguardz Unequal Shock iPhone 6 Plus Case
text:
I bought this case without examining it too closely after having an Unequal Shock case on my iPhone 6 Plus.

Buyers in similar circumstance should note that there is a significant design change for the iPhone 7 Plus which you may want to consider prior to purchasing.

The iPhone 6 Plus case had raised buttons to control the phone's sleep/power and volume up/down buttons.

The iPhone 7 Plus version does not include these raised buttons, which at first was a huge problem for me. It was very difficult to find the spot on the case to press in order to activate the volume up or volume down button by feel. There are tiny raised "+" and "-" markings over these buttons, but it seems as if you'd need fingertips as sensitive as a safecracker's to be able to "read" the marks by feel.

After a few days of complaining about this, I realized that instead of groping around the side of the case for the button I wanted, I can first locate the cut-out over the hardware mute switch, and then move my finger down the side of the case 1/4" or so for volume up or 3/4" for volume down, and find the correct spot to press that way. This takes a moment longer than with the raised buttons on the 6 Plus case, but it works much better than trying to read the "+" and "-" by feel.

The sleep/power button offers a similar challenge, but I haven't had as much trouble with that one, possibly because there's only the one button on that side of the case.

I haven't dropped my phone yet, but this case does seem to offer decent protection, with a much slimmer profile than the OtterBox Commuter case I used on my previous Samsung Note 3. The Commuter's two part construction offered a slightly grippier texture on the parts of the case where the soft inner case was exposed, but I am optimistic that the texture on the edges of the Unequal Shock case will be sufficient to keep the phone from slipping out of my grasp.

In case you might be tempted, as I was, to try the iPhone 6 Plus case on the iPhone 7 Plus, be aware that the camera opening will not be large enough. If you have a very steady hand and a very sharp knife, you might be able to modify the 6 Plus case yourself. I didn't look past the camera opening problem to determine whether the buttons on the 6 Plus case line up with the buttons on the iPhone 7, but I believe they probably do.

After this experience I have a much better appreciation for those with visual impairments who read by Braille.
label: positive

text:
This power bank is ultimately replacing the older one I have with less capacity. In that respect, this should do that handily. I plugged it into charge in the USB-C and it took over 8 hours to get from 32% to 100%. That is after it stalled at 86% for over an hour. I eventually plugged it into a different charger to see if it made any difference. Doing that must have reset it or something as the percentage started increasing again. Both chargers work perfectly on multiple devices so it's not an issue with the chargers. I put my phone(Galaxy S20) on to charge and it took less than 30 minutes to fast-charge from 85% to 100%. So, it charges devices fairly quickly and only dropped 2% during that charge.
Now for the not so good... While I didn't get this for the "super bright light," I would have been quite disappointed if I had. The light barely illuminates the instructions printed for ants. The nexus line really didn't have a solid premium offering that competed with the current carrier based premium handsets until now with the Nexus 6P. To put this to the test I also bought a AT&T variant of the Samsung S7 Edge. I tested both phones for 2 weeks before returning the S7 edge back to Best Buy. Both phone performed well, but I didn't see spending an additional $400 for the S7 Edge as money well spent. The 6P seemed to run smoother even with almost 1 year old hardware than the S7 edge. A testament to stock Android optimization. I know from experience that this performance gap will also be maintained as the 6p will continue to receive the latest OS updates. Outside of a few niggles I have like the power button and volume rocker switch placement, the 6p is a total winner for the price. Bye bye contracts, slow updates, and locked bootloaders. title: Don't buy direct from i-Blason!
text:
This is a fine case, especially to get you started with protecting your new iPhone 6. It's made of a flexible, clear polymer. The one that is clear all the way around was my choice; it ranges from crystal clear when looking at the back, to jellyfish-like cloudy when looking at the edges while the phone is lying flat.

Every case presents a tradeoff, starting with the fact that you have to hide your new device behind something. This kind of case, for me, minimizes the number of tradeoffs I have to make. It lets me still see the phone, and that's a great start. It also is made of a pleasant material that lets me feel I have a better grip on the device.. another plus. If you like your phone's appearance enough to preserve it, this is the right case type for you.

Unfortunately, my case came with a manufacturing defect. The case bows outward on the right side ever so slightly, making it look like the case is loosely clinging to the phone on that side. It's slight, but noticeable, and it makes me wonder if this case might have been in someone else's hands before. Every time I look at the case, I think "This an i-Blason case, and from the first moment, it didn't fit properly." I had plans to do what I've done with Amazon in the past: file for an exchange. Amazon sends a new one of the same item, then when you get it you stick the old one in the envelope and send it back. No luck, though, if your case wasn't "sold by Amazon.com". If i-Blason sold it to you through Amazon's site, you have to handle the shipping yourself, and I have no idea if you get any of the shipping costs refunded for the defective product. So I'm keeping what could easily have been a five-star case but, thanks to a combination of luck of the draw and a very 20th century return policy, I'm giving it a tough-but-fair two stars.

title: Too small for my ear when wearing eyeglasses
text:
I've had the Voyager Legend Pro the version before that and they both fit fine. Unfortunately they went through the laundry so I wanted a more water resistant headset. I've been using this newer version for over a month now and unfortunately it is too small for my ear, especially when I wear my eyeglasses. This is why I give it 3 stars. I can sortof get it to fit by first removing my eyeglasses while putting on the headset. I then have to rotate the headset about 20 degrees clockwise from its natural position to get the earbud into my ear canal. Then I can put my glasses back on, but I wear them partially askew since there is not enough room on top of my right ear for both the headset and the eyeglass frame, so the over-ear part of the eyeglass frame sits partially on top of the headset. Even doing this, headset feels small & loose, but does not fall off. Changing the earbud piece does not help. For the record, I'm not a huge person with elephant ears, I'm 6'2" and 170lbs.

On the plus side, the sound quality is good and the battery life is pretty good too. I'd say about 5 hours of continuous talk time. Also, the headset does not hurt my ear after long wear, but I wish the plastic/rubber piece that fits into the ear canal were a tad softer and more pliable.

I think Plantronics needs to think about having different size headsets or make them more adjustable somehow.

Had the overhang been on one side only, then it could be assumed that this was due to the shield not being placed in the exact center.

I contacted the customer support, and they were prompt and helpful in getting me a replacement. They mentioned "The technicians will test the design on the physical device to ensure quality and fitment before approving the design for production. The technicians use the same method a consumer would to install the protectors." Therefore, it was suggested that I possibly received a defective protector.

I am really happy to say the replacement fits great! These types of shields offer more protection then the tradition screen protectors. They also provide better grip and don't smudge as easily. Excellent clarity too.

It is noted on the documentation that the bubbles (if any) should disappear within 24 hours. However, a couple of bubbles took 3-4 days to completely disappear. Once gone, the finish was perfect. These types of protectors are also far easier to apply, and you also have little chance of getting misalignment and dirt/fiber trapped during placement, compared to traditional screen protectors.

I recommend this product due to the quality, protection, and great customer service.

title: Seemed solid at first
text:
Update September 25th 2022: this battery is garbage. Today I use the phone to navigate for miles. I did about a half an hour of surfing the web and the battery went from 100% to 43% just like that. Huge bummer. Hope it lasts till Christmas.

I was looking for an inexpensive phone for myself and then another one to purchase for my mother. After being unsuccessful with another slightly more expensive phone that did not operate properly I came upon the reviews for this phone and decided to give it a shot.

I would say so far mostly good. Right out of the box the talk to text works much more smoothly than Samsung a53. There's a lot more on the keyboard for this phone so I find myself getting a little lost trying to figure out how to get the keyboard to come back etc but generally it's been easier to operate and I appreciate that the microphone and the keyboard can be displayed simultaneously.

The fingerprint reader is fairly worthless, almost never works but I have a very sturdy case it can making it tricky to jam your finger in there. Seems like maybe not the best idea to have it where it is and then you end up limited to only using your right hand so not so great for lefties like me.

Battery life is okay. I'm satisfied with that. It seems to go down to 80% pretty quick but that range in between 80% and it's when it's below 50 seems like it takes a little longer. I had hoped it would be better and it seemed to be better the first few weeks but capacity may have gone done significnatly in a short time. Also noticed that the charging cable and block charges slowly but if I put on my old pixel changer it is rapid charging, not sure why it wouldn't be the other way around.

As another reviewer mentioned, on the Verizon network you might have a little trouble receiving texts. I did it first, I didn't do anything to change it except for one of the updates that I was prompted to do and then suddenly they came in. I'll keep an eye on that. I'm going to try and update as I discover more about this phone. I will say in general getting around on this phone is a little trickier than my old pixel XL. Like trying to go back seems to only happen with a swipe to the right. Trying to toggle between different apps was also tricky. What I figured out was that you have to go into settings, navigation and then turn off gestures to get the three buttons at the bottom for back, reduce app, and then to show all open apps.

.Also trying to get my apps that I do not have icons on the screen for yet is a little tricky... Seems like if you start swiping from 3/4 down the screen and up you will get them which is too similar to swiping from all the way at the bottom of the screen which does something totally different. Trying to get the app icons onto the home screen into a shared bubble is almost like a video game. Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't.

Update- this was fixed with system update: Something that's starting to happen that's concerning me is that I'm realizing it's rebooting and updating software nightly. Tonight it did it twice and wakes me up at 1:00 a.m. and then again it almost two with "hello Moto"after it's done updating. I don't know why it needs such frequent updates and I'm beginning to think it's a bit of a glitch. This would be the second phone that I had from Amazon in a row that seems glitchy so I'm not sure if these phones are new or used and refurbished. Hopefully these are all about some setting I need to figure out how to adjust.

title: Not bad, but could be a lot better
text:
I really needed a case for my Sprint GN2 and have always been a fan of this style of convertible cases. I've used them with tablets in the past and they worked rather well. First, the materials appear to be rather nice. Just holding the case it feels well built, descent grip, not slippery, and even has an almost leather-like odor to it. Not bad at all.

And because the back/front and 4 corners are covered, you even have a descent amount of protection. This leaves all of the buttons and ports easily accessible. The case is nice and sturdy, and as a result, does add some noticeably bulk, easily doubling the thickness. But you can see that from the pictures. No surprises there. It has all of the expected openings for phone, mic, and even the stylus. Although it is a tad trickier to get to the stylus since the cut-out isn't as big as would like. Could be an issues for larger fingers.

However, out of the box, the phone didn't quite fit all that well in the case. I had to bend the 4 grips just so that it would stop popping out so much. Now it's much better, but not as "tight" as I would like it to be. It's not going to fall out or anything. And at least the phone is very easy to take in and out of the case. The cover and leather covered clasp both fit and work very well. With a little practice, you can even open it with one hand.

The "convertible" portion works as expected. Just flip it up and set it in landscape mode and away you go. It has an indention to help keep it propped up in one angle. Although because this phone is so light, I've found you can pretty much put it in any angle you want. And with the new design they have, you no longer have to partially remove it from it's holder to do this.

The big issue I have is that there is no indention in the cover for the front Home button. So anytime there is pressure applied to the front of the case, the button is pressed and the phone is turned on. So if it's in a pocket, bag, or if you just happen to squeeze a at the wrong spot, you could have some issues. That's a pretty big oversight in my mind.

Also as mentioned above, the new convertible design that allows you to easily switch to landscape mode, also means there is much less support for the cover when it's open. Meaning it'll move around a lot more when not securely closed. Not a big deal, but worth noting.

PROS:
+ New more efficient convertible case design
+ Good quality materials
+ Moderate phone protection
+ Nice feel & ergonomics
+ Easy case removal
+ Cheap!

CONS:
- Poor fitment out of the box
- No home button indention
- Loose cover when open
- Small cut-out for stylus

Overall, when you take into consideration it's form, functionality, and especially price, it's really not bad. But the lack of home button indention and less than ideal fit are big negatives for me and will unfortunately prevent me from using it as much as I'd like. Otherwise, for such a cheap case, I'll keep it around and use it occasionally when not traveling.

title: SOLUTION to Clock on screen when phone is in magnetic holder
text: I bought this for my wife's LG-G4. At first it was unusable because putting the phone into the case made the phone have a clock on it. You could answer calls but you could not browse or do other full screen things because the display was limited to a circle that showed a clock or some icons. After a LOT of browsing I found that this is a special mode for the "quick circle case" made by LG. The "quick circle case" works by having the phone detect a magnet when the phone is closed and only a circle shows through the closed case. This Cellularvilla causes the phone to detect a magnet when the case is either open or closed. The only way to cause the phone not to detect the magnet is remove the phone. That was not acceptable to my wife. I found that you go to Settings -> General -> Smart Functions -> Quick Circle Case (TURN IT OFF). Then the phone works in the case without removing it from its magnetic holder. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is that I'm worried that the magnet won't hold when the phone is dropped. But all in all it's a nice product.

title: Great Until It Doesn't Work, Then You Have No Phone Until LG Repairs It
text:
When it works, the phone is perfectly fine. But within the first 60 days I began getting alerts that there was moisture in the USB (charging) port. Odd, since it hadn't been anywhere near moisture. Checked online forums and found this was a frequent complaint . Most often it can be resolved by removing lint from the port using fine tweezers, a toothpick (or some similar small object), or blowing it out with canned compressed air. Now the phone is 4 months old, and it has started to re-boot un-commanded, usually several times an a row, then it stops for a few days. And in the last several days, it sometimes won't charge (tried multiple USB connectors, same result).

So I called LG for assistance. They had me do a factory reset, but the problems and alerts continue. So they offered to send me an RMA to send the phone in for repair or replacement. But unlike most reputable manufacturers, they won't send a replacement first - you have no phone while they're repairing or deciding to replace yours. As this phone has a less-than-stellar reputation for reliability, it's not unlikely that you're going to need it fixed or replaced under warranty - and you'll be totally without a phone for a week, give or take. With this sort of support, I really can't recommend ANY phone from LG.

text:
Controllers and tracking: tracking is great for the most part, I used this headset for a full playthrough of superhot VR and the only issue I had is that it was hard to throw things from time to time because the controllers would lose tracking and the item would just drop to the ground. The overall feel of the controllers is very good, they are plastic but very durable. I have punched them into my walls a few times and they still work great. One issue I have with them is that the trackpad is VERY sensitive and activates even when you are not touching it, this was a big issue for games like vrchat and my emotes kept going off for no reason.

Material quality and look: Everything looks very nice and the material feels good, my only complaint is the facemask material which leads me into comfort.

Comfort: Everything except the facemask is very comfortable and the controllers have a very nice feel, the face mask issue can also be easily fixed by buying a different one (they're pretty cheap). Aside from that my only other gripe is that I wish the headphones could come off or could come down onto your ears a bit more.

Picture quality: On my computer, the picture quality looks great, but in the headset, it is quite a low res, and ipd and positioning of the headset must be almost perfect to be able to read text from further than 3 feet away. (also depending on the size of the text and font) The edges of the lenses are also quite blurry so you have to move your whole head to read the text, though this was easy to get used to and is no bother at all.

Overall, I had a very good first VR experience with this headset but the picture quality and comfort bugged me a little bit, and once you get over the hype of the first time VR experience, those issues only become more prevalent. If the picture quality had a way to be changed to a useful degree I would make this rating a 4-5 star.

title: Pretty good.
text:
Okay, first... for all the "1-star-because-I-can't-read" folks... This product fits perfectly on the Galaxy S7 ACTIVE....

What's good
- Snug fit. Rubber back seems flexible enough and didn't stretch out of whack when installing for a test fit. I removed and replaced 3x no issues.
- Fingerprint sensor works
- Menu pull-down, right/left swipe work just fine.

What could be better
- Lower portion of the faceplate is a little robust considering the active has physical buttons at the bottom instead of touch points. It's fine, but if you have dexterity issues or really large fingers you might have an issue pushing the buttons.
- Side buttons take a little more effort than I think they intended. When the front faceplate is snapped on, the buttons are slightly off-center up and down (closer to the "back" of the hole in relation to the phone front and back).
- Extra flap covers for the power and headphone port work fine but are overkill for a phone that is already waterproof. I may end up cutting them off. But... They do work as intended.

The belt clip part works fine but honestly I'll probably never use it. That said, the clip does rotate as described. It "locks in" every 30 degrees so there are 12 position choices for you. I do wish they had designed it so you could put the phone in with the screen facing out. That might be more useful to me to hang the phone where I can get to it when I'm working with my hands.

Last thought. I didn't get paid for this review, I just hate it when I try to read the reviews on stuff and they're written by confused or disgruntled folks.

One last thought... I have a hardened glass screen protector so I ripped out the little plastic built-in screen protector. Still works fine but fits better due to the thickness of the glass.

title: Relatively Expensive, Not For The Impatient
text:
This is the BMW of screen protectors. The installation process is not rocket science but for that impatient younger person or the adult with ADD, you can easily screw things up if you don't closely follow the instructions. There seems to be an obsession with glass protectors. I found this one to be basically overpriced because of all the install parts that it comes with. You get more scratch resistance but I prefer the high-quality TPU protectors that feel just like glass and you just replace them every once in a while at about $5 a piece. They look just as good and are less prone to fingerprint sensitivity issues. See Ringke Easy Dual Wing for example. As with all protectors though, the reviews will be either 5-star or 1-star typically reflecting no user-error or user-error during install. I don't like having to pour liquid glue on my phones.

While the downside of the TPU/EPU protectors is less scratch resistance (but they are disposable), the typically cover more of the curved edges. This one doesn't cover the curved edge on the S23 Ultra. So thumbs down considering the high price. But the Whitestone fanboys will still buy it.

title: Unusable - assembled wrong?
text:
I have to assume I received a dud because I don't see this issue in any other review - the unit I received appears to have been installed wrong!

The hinge only allows the ring to open up in one direction. In my case, that's towards the adhesive pad that is supposed to attach to the device. Which means that once it's attached, the ring becomes useless. Also, there is absolutely no twist happening to allow the alleged 360° rotation.

The listing claims this is 2.9mm thick. Maybe the metal/plastic part is, but once the adhesive foam pad is included (and it's pre-attached on mine), the actual thickness is 3.5mm. Almost 20% more than advertised. That leaves a rather significant gap between the edge of the ring and the device it's mounted to, so I'm honestly not surprised at the reviews where the ring broke off in a purse or pocket.

The only positive thing I can say about this listing is that they provided two clear plastic adhesive discs that you attach directly to your phone or case before adhering the mount (a small card inside the packaging notes that you have to use these for a phone with a glass body like the iPhone X or with oil painting or matte finishes).

You will want to make sure that it is the right kind of case for your needs, check to make sure it fits properly, and make sure that it is what you are actually looking for. If you work in more “hostile” environment, you will want a more durable case. If you only need it for around the house, you will likely be more comfortable with a case that is small and protects only against every day wear and tear like scratches and such. Finding the right case for you may prove to be a difficult task, but it will be worth it to find a case that you are happy with instead of a case that you are settling for. title: Beautiful Phone with problems, and Does Not Support Mac
text:
** HTC does NOT offer sync software for Mac OS for this phone. I have tried two 3rd party sync programs that do not work.

PROS:

1. The phone is very pretty. The screen has vibrant colors.

2. The larger form factor is a plus. I don't want to go back to anything smaller now. However, my wife thinks it is too big.

CONS:

1. No sync with Mac. This is a deal breaker for me. It does appear on the finder as a drive if you select "connect as disk drive." You can drag and drop music files onto the phone. But contacts, calendar, to-dos, notes, etc. do not sync.

2. Battery life is average to poor. Worse, the phone seems slow to charge.

3. The apps are badly organized in my opinion. This makes it difficult for a new android user.

4. The multi-touch gestures are laggy. For example, pinch a website and there is a pause from the time you pinch to the time the screen moves. This is a little frustrating.

5. There is something funny about where or how the speaker is positioned. If you don't hold the phone exactly right to your ear you can only hear a little teeny tiny sound. This makes answering in a hurry difficult.

6. I am not a phone camera buff, but still was disappointed in the quality of the pictures given the cost and how current the technology is. It takes too many steps to get the pictures into iPhoto.

7. My 2010 Mercedes C300 recognizes the phone by bluetooth, and it will answer calls (after pairing, which took 5-6 attempts to complete). However it will not allow use of other phone features by bluetooth including dialing out. This is also a deal breaker.

For essentially the same price as an iPhone, this phone is a terrible deal. I have awful buyer's remorse about it. I cannot recommend this phone.

title: Using a Foreign Carrier's SIM Card Can Be Complicated
text: When I purchased this SIM card with a pre-paid 30 day plan, I was aware that I would not be able to call or text the United States, (at least, not with the plan that came with the SIM card). I wanted to be able to access the internet, and be able to call and text my brother and his wife, who I was traveling with to 4 countries in Europe on a Viking Rhine River cruise. My brother and his wife at first bought SIM cards for their phones (another brand) at the Schiphol airport in Amsterdam. They had so much trouble trying to get their phones to work that they put their original SIM cards back in and used an overseas plan provided by their United States carrier that charged $10.00 a day. They were able to call and text me and each other, but I couldn't call or text them. I attempted to put some money on my "Three" SIM card account (thinking that this would allow me to call and text my brother and his wife). I used the "Three" application I installed on my phone, as well as also using their website, but in either case I was not able to do it. I wasn't able to get past a question on the form that asked for my "Post Code". I'm not sure what they were asking here. I filled in my zip code for my U.S. address, but this didn't work. I got so frustrated that I eventually gave up. I could still access the internet, and I was able to make a call to the Viking Cruises long ship that I was a passenger on. I was also able to be called by my brother and his wife, and receive texts from them, but I couldn't answer the texts. In addition to this, I eventually learned that we would all need to add the country code of the carrier (to the beginning of the phone number we were calling) regardless of what country we were in at the time. If my brother wanted to call me, as an example, even if we were in the Netherlands, he would have to add +44 (the UK country code) to the beginning of my phone number, since I was using the SIM card of a phone carrier that was based in the UK. And since my brother was using his U.S. carrier's SIM card I would have to add a +1 (the U.S. country code) to the beginning of his phone number, if I called him. I never knew that using my phone in Europe would be so complicated.

title: As others have said - too narrow
text:
This glass is *exactly* as wide as the Pixel 7 screen and has to be perfectly centered to minimize or eliminate edge distortions. Too bad you can't use the enclosed guide as that sets the glass too low and the top of the screen peeks over the top of the glass with distortion.

If you want to give it a try anyway:
1) Ditch the alignment guide
2) If you look closely at the bottom, you can see where the deep black bezel and lighter black of the screen begins.
3) Lay the glass edge at the bottom of the phone, about 1mm below the bezel/screen line
4) Center the glass across the width of the phone (it is as wide as the screen, so a little left or right will create distortion
5) Let the glass drop, squeeze or lift and press to remove bubbles
6) In the end the glass should be centered left to right and slightly closer to the top than the bottom.
