title: Pretty Case but Poor Protection and Functionality, Plus Horrible Service
text:
1/5 Stars

I was debating buying this case, one of Spigen's Tough Armor cases or an Otterbox and ultimately decided to go with the Slim Armor in the Metal Slate color because of its attractive design and color and the generally extremely positive reviews, plus I was able to pick it up from Spigen's eBay store several dollars cheaper than on Amazon and for half the price of the other cases. This purchase was a mistake because a case should make one feel that one's very expensive smartphone is more secure and this one makes me feel that it is LESS secure than using no case, in a rather important way. I was debating whether to rate this a 1/5 or if a 2/5 would be more fair, but given this case's significant problems caused by its designers' focus on style over functionality, I plan on replacing it immediately with something better; I figure that a product that is so flawed that it requires me to replace it immediately does not deserve even a 2/5 rating.

PROS:

- It's very attractive with the deep metallic navy midsection/back contrasting nicely with the black rubber top and bottom.

- Power and volume buttons feel decent and work properly. The sliding mute button above the volume buttons is tricky to get to but the cutout is just big enough if I use a fingernail; guys with bigger hands will likely find the cutout too small, though. Maybe I have a newer version of the case with a bigger cutout on the bottom, but contrary to what some older critical reviews have reported, I've had no problems using both the Apple and a generic Lightning power cord.

- Slim design for those who desparately want a razor-slim case (but most of them ironically wish Apple had added at least an extra inch to the screen size, rendering it a near-tablet size behemoth like some of the latest-greatest Android phones that won't fit into a pocket. However, I digress....)

- The case fits snugly enough to be secure without any loose space but not so tight it is difficult to remove the phone when needed.

- The case appears to have some sort of rubber air pocket shock protection in the corners, so it likely would fair better in a drop than a $6 hard plastic or silicone sleeve case.

CONS:

- First and foremost, the blue metallic plastic that makes up 80% of the case's body is extremely slippery. There is absolutely no reason for the case to be so slippery because with a semi-matte finish to it, Spigen could easily have added some texture to it without worrying about ruining a glossy shine. Holding it in the middle of the case with anything less than at least double the firmness I held my old HTC One V will result in the phone slipping out of my fingers. In fact, in the first hour I used the case, it actually did slip out of my fingers, but I was lucky enough to be picking it up off my bed and it fell back on the soft bed rather than on the floor. I'll admit that I have fairly dry skin, but I really can't believe more people haven't commented very negatively about this phone's lack of a secure surface to grip rendering it easily more slick to hold than a bare iPhone. With the 5s having a fairly long screen and with the Cancel and back-one-screen icons coming up in the top left of the screen, it is a bit of a reach to get to them operating the phone with one hand and a slippery case makes that more difficult. My wife has a custom photo case she ordered for her 5s that is also smooth, but it has a slightly soft, rubbery feel to it and gripping that case is no problem at all. I am confident that if I continued to use this case, I would be dropping it at least once a week and eventually breaking my brand new 5s. I have a hard rubber case I bought from the US Cellular store for my old HTC One V that has a very secure, tacky grip, but it's not so sticky as to be a problem putting it in or pulling it out from a pocket; unfortunately, it has no name on the case itself, I long ago threw away the packaging, and US Cellular does not carry them any more, so I cannot figure out who the manufacturer is and if the company makes a similar case for my 5s.

- The lip edge around the screen is too low and won't adequately protect the screen. Spigen's product listing has the edge at about .8mm above the level of the screen and that is only about 30% of the height it should be, especially with a screen protector on the screen, which brings the screen height nearly even with the edge of the case. The case on my old HTC has a lip that's about 2.5mm high and that height is perfect, tall enough to provide plenty of protection if laid down on a slightly uneven surface and, combined with the slightly flexible rubber material, it will bend and absorb shock if it lands face down in a fall, whereas I think the result of a face-down fall with this Slim Armor case will be a broken screen. I'm not some frenzied texter who is forming tendinitis of the thumbs, but I never found my old case's prominent lip edge to get in the way of entering text into my old phone.

- There is a very prominent and sharp edge running vertically both front and back on both side corner edges of the blue plastic midsection of the case. This sharp edges add neither function nor visible style to the case and are simply pointlessly uncomfortable. They don't cause pain, but the case would be more comfortable to use if they were rounded off on the corners instead of sharp.

- Does not appear to be sturdy enough to last more than maybe one fall from above 4' onto a hard floor. I think one might get a single save out of the case if it landed on a corner or bottom side edge, but I doubt this would survive repeated drops. Lesser durability is a natural trade-off with a slimmer case, though.

- The blue plastic midsection of the case does not fit particularly well at the junction with the black softer top portion of the case, just under the camera and the midsection sticks up slighly , maybe half the height of the raised lip edge on the front of the case around the screen.

- The hard plastic midsection of the case scratches very easily. I've had my phone in my case for less than half a day and already it's got two rather noticeable scratches on it and I can't recall doing anything at all with the case that would have brought it into contact with something hard that could have scratched it.

- The cutout for the mute switch immediately above the volume buttons would be too small for really large fingers to access (I could just get the tip of my index finger nail in there and I typically wear size Men's L gloves). However, that is a button that should be protected against accidentally sliding it, so this is a pretty minor gripe.

- Spigen's shipping was pretty slow. I bought some Lightning cables from an Amazon affiliated vendor a day AFTER I purchased this Spigen case, both the cables and the case shipped via USPS First Class Mail from California, and I got the cables two days BEFORE the case arrived. Not an issue if you buy from Amazon and use Prime, but if you read a bunch of reviews for this case, pretty much anyone who comments on any aspect of Spigen's customer service has noted that it ranges from mediocre to truly awful.

CONCLUSION:

This is a pretty case but it simply doesn't do well most of the things that every smartphone case should do. Spigen's designers clearly chose style over form and substance when they planned this product and made some questionable decisions when they could have made the case work much better without significantly altering its appearance. Since I plan on shopping for a new case to replace this Slim Armor at lunch today, after less than 24 hours of use, it should come as no surprise that I don't recommend this Spigen product.

I ended up replacing this case with a Tactic case by Body Glove and am very happy with the new case. The Tactic is very slightly bigger than the Slim Armor, but feels a lot sturdier and damage resistant, plus it has a ribbed rubber side of the case that offers excellent grip but still leaves the back of the case smooth and shiny (but no scratches) to slip easily into one's pocket. AND, the Body Glove Tactic is about $5 cheaper than this Spigen case.

EPILOGUE:

So after publishing this 1/5 review of their product, Spigen posted a comment to my review with a link to their customer service urging me to contact them so they could try to do something to make me a happy customer. So I did send them an e-mail through their link.

No response.

Shortly thereafter, Spigen's eBay store sent me one of those beg-a-thon messages asking me to give them positive feedback or to contact them if I had a problem with the purchase. So I did and sent them a second e-mail.

No response to that one, either.

It's been a good 10 days or so and no response from Spigen to either e-mail. Clearly they have no intention of responding. I suppose that their only intent in sending out those e-mails is to attempt to generate a false impression that they are a company that cares and that takes care of their customers.

There are hundreds of negative feedbacks for Spigen's eBay store. Probably half of them mention the same thing that I experienced, namely, that Spigen customer service refuses to respond to communications from customers.

A whole bunch of other feedbacks are complaining about extremely slow shipping. Furthermore, a lot of other feedbacks are stating not just that their Spigen cases scratch easily, but that Spigen sent them a case that was already scratched, i.e. a used case. What kind of company doesn't ever respond to customer inquiries and then sells people used, damaged products under the pretext of selling them new ones?

The answer to that last question is a crappy company. A really, really, really crappy company that doesn't care a whit about customer service.

title: Worked Great Until It Broke.
text:
ETA:
Contacted seller, they promptly sent me a new one. Same potential problems but I appreciate the attempt. Changed my rating from one to three stars.

Short Story:
Looked promising. Good price at $14.49. Ordered March 22 2016, shipped March 23, arrived March 29th, broke April 4 2016.

A major problem here I think is the iPhone 6s is a large phone to put on a belt clip. Add the Otterbox Resurgence to that and it borders on ungainly. I hate putting the phone in my pants pocket so I was willing to give it a shot. I was pleased to see a belt clip holster was available. When it arrived it looked well made. Somebody designed this to specifically fit the Resurgence and I think they did a fine job in the fit of the phone to the holster.

The problem lies with the belt clip. I do like that it rotates, that's a big plus. Unfortunately that makes for a smaller attachment point between the clip to the plate of the holster. This clip does look fairly well made and probably works great on smaller phones but it is the weak point here and that is exactly where it failed.

I now have 2 parts. The backing plate/ holster and the clip. If I would have rated this yesterday I would have given it a 4. I was still trying to find the best place for me to clip it. 9 O'clock position and it stuck out too far, 10-11 interfered with my bending. The 7-8 O'clock position seemed best but the testing of positions didn't last very long at all as it broke.

If the clip attachment to the plate was made more robust I think this holster just might work, then again, the size of the iPhone 6 along with the Otterbox Resurgence is quite the challenge for this type of holster.

Overall, 3 stars. Here's why: as a case it does its job. This thing protects your phone and seems to be well built. It's also way thinner than an otterbox so the 6s plus actually fits in your pocket. However, all the nice smooth lines of the case have a tendency to slip out of your hand if you're not being careful. The aluminum shell also drops your GPS accuracy down from (and this is only in my experience. It doesn't necessarily mean it'll happen to you) a 5 meter horizontal and 3 meter vertical accuracy to a 65 to 200 meter horizontal and 10 meter vertical accuracy. That means that for everyday gps navigation it'll still work if you're navigating around in a small city or on the highway but if you're in a city with tall buildings or lots of small NYC style city blocks your ability to precisely navigate will be fairly degraded.

Also, if you're using your phone as a speedometer (which is more than likely illegal and should only be used to aid in situational awareness) your actual speed will not be anything close to accurate.

As far as cell reception goes, I'm noticing a slight decline in service but I have sprint so who knows what will happen on your network. It's not terrible but I'm not thrilled about it either...

All in all, it's a solid case that will be great for situations where I don't want my giant otterbox. I call this case my "goin out case" since it's small enough to fit in my jeans pocket. However, if I want to navigate a large city or go on a backpacking adventure I'll have to find something else.

title: TERRIBLE glue gun!
text:
I hate to give any product a bad review. It is not something I take lightly. I use a glue gun daily for my work and have for over 5 years. I ordered this one because the reviews seemed good and it has smaller nozzle than the one I'd had before. I hoped it would be better for the fine details I work with. I was wrong.

PROS:
The hottest setting does get really hot if that's what you need. It's nice to be able to switch between temps. Seems like a sturdy gun.

CONS:
It spits glue all over the place! It eats glue sticks like crazy. I have used both the sticks that came with the gun and ones I bought at Walmart. No difference. At times, it seems stuck with nothing coming out and then all of the sudden, glue comes gushing out and won't stop. NOT good when you are in the middle of doing a fine detail and scalding hot glue is pouring out with no control! I normally go through about 1 glue stick every 4-5 days. With this gun, I am going through 2 PER DAY! Glue doesn't just drip out when it's sitting and not in use....it POURS out in puddles. And the strings! Oh my! It doesn't matter what setting it is on, the strings are awful. I expect strings from hot glue, but I have never had a gun with this amount of strings. I've tried the sticks that came with it and also the ones I bought elsewhere. Same result. So much of the glue comes out brown or dark yellow. That's also not what I want for the items I make. I need CLEAR glue. I had no problem with that with other glue guns I used...no matter what type of glue sticks I used in them. I really wanted this gun to work for me. I have tried to give it a chance, and now I am wishing I had returned it. It's disheartening to spend money on something that I can't even use. See the pic I attached for what my glue gun table looks like after only a couple of days. I just cleaned the table a few days ago, and no the glue gun is not left on continuously. I have it on a smart plug and only turn it on when I am working.

text: So, I absolutely love the idea of having a fine tip option for the apple pencil since I do a lot of artwork on my iPad pro and think the nibs that come with it and that are sold everywhere else are way too bulky. The first of these flaws was the fact that the small, impossible to locate if you drop one, tip covers that you have to use unless you want to be dragging a metal tip all over your screen/ screen protector are slightly hard to put on the tip but that's not their biggest flaw, if that was the only issue I could definitely overlook that. The big problem is that they wear through SO quickly! Granted I do have a paper feel screen protector that is textured and will wear down nibs quicker than a smooth surface, that being said, they shouldn't wear completely through to the point that the metal is scratching up my screen protector that had to be replaced after, and not just once. I'm on my 4th screen protector because of these. I have gone through as many as 3 of these tip covers in the span of one drawing session (3-4 hours). And I'm not so much upset about the rate at which I go though then as much as what happens when I'm in the middle of drawing and one wears out. The metal fine tip nib puts deep scratches into my not cheap screen protector that is ruined when that happens. My second major issue is the fact that one of these two nibs just completely stopped working about 3 hours into being used and has not worked since. If I had to do it again I definitely wouldn't purchase these exact fine tip nibs. I'm hoping there are more and better quality options for smaller nibs available soon because now I'm back to the original bulky ones because I just can't afford to keep replacing screen protectors because of this product :(

title: Consider the SR-60 Instead
text:
These are supposed to use the same drivers as the Grado SR-60, and I have both, but side-by-side, the iGrado sounds somewhat weedy and thin. They still sound pretty good for the price, but not as good as other Grado cans. They are also pretty uncomfortable. The plastic behind-the-neck headband is not adjustable and presses into your skull in an awkward way. After using them for several weeks at work, I did adapt to them, but other headphones are just more comfortable. The cord is also thinner and less durable than the SR-60.

The comparison might be unfair - the SR-60 is both legendary and exquisite. But it's only a $20 difference.

They are more portable than other Grados, but they don't fold flat, or collapse like some other portable headphones. They're also cheaper, and even though they don't sound quite as good, they're still a pretty radical upgrade over the ear-buds that came with your iPod.

I would recommend these if:
1) Your headphone budget is $50, and you can't stretch it to $70.
2) The SR-60 is not light and portable enough.
3) You don't care for the retro-space-cadet look of other Grado cans, or just need to get white headphones to match your MP3 player.
4) You have big hair and would benefit from the behind-the-neck design.

Otherwise, the extra $20 for a pair of SR-60s is worth it. A nice pair of headphones will last you many years; getting the right pair is worth a few extra bucks.

title: Best phone for the price
text:
I have had my LG Dare for nearly a year now and I love it. I find the touch screen is easy to use and it has the features I value. I bought an unlimited data and text plan. The web browsing is really great and the display looks good, too. The zoom feature on the browser is very handy. I also use VZ navigator a lot both at home and when I travel. The camera resolution is OK but, of course, the lens is not so great and I find the focus is usually pretty soft unless in bright light. I did not buy it for the camera however.

Here is my take on the features I use the most.

Telephone:
Sound quality: as good as most phones I have had which have mostly been LG phones as well
Dailing ease: The buttons are easy to use and of good size.
Contacts: Lots of room and good layout, easy to add and edit.

Web browser and Vcast Video:
I am really impressed with the speed and display size/quality
Favorites are easy to use unless you want to rename something with a long name, then it is a pain.
Zoom works really well
It is nice to have this entertainment at your finger tips for long waits at the doctor's office, etc.

VZ Navigator
I truly love this feature both nav and local search
Lots of helpful features
It could default to the number keys when you enter a zip code, though.
Maps seem to be pretty accurate and up to date

MP3 Player
I keep my music on a Micro SD, the sound quality is not as good as a stand alone MP3 but it is convenient to have this feature in one package. I can be listening to music and take a call with the same blue tooth headset.

Email
This is not the greatest but at least I can deal with anything that needs a fast and short response. If you need to get HTML emails on a mobile device this is not the one for you.

Texting
I think it is exceptionally good becuase of the full QWERTY touch screen keyboard.

I like this phone very much, so I buy a lot of accessories for it.
*Charger for the car. I have attached a USB hub to the charger so I can charge my other devices while traveling.
*Dash mounted holder to make using VZ Navigator more convenient[[ASIN:B000IEGQ56 Apple iPod mini nano mp3 player Sony Ericsson Motorola Nokia Samsung LG phone car / auto mount universal vent + dash holder GPS navigation]]
*Protective screen overlay[[ASIN:B001DNOI3S LG VX9700 Dare ClearTouch Crystal Screen Protectors (3-Pack)]]
*Stylus that attaches with a small layard to the phone (why not include one, LG?)[[ASIN:B0028YFQ5U elago Retractable Stylus with Removable Strap for Touchscreen wireless phone (Black)]]
*Leather holster
*8Gb Micro SD for Music and pictures
*BlueTrek Duo Bluetooth headset (I recommend this device, too)[[ASIN:B001SAU26I Bluetrek DUO Stereo Bluetooth Headset]]

title: Great phone mount with nice visual design
text:
I recently got rather fed up with the frequency at which suction mount keeps falling out of windshield. So I decided to get this car mount for center console. Presentation wise, the phone mount comes inside a nice Vava box, giving it a premium feel. By the way, this can be a great Christmas gift for your loved ones.

The installation is straightforward. You clean the surface on your center console with the supplied alcohol wipe, and proceed to take off the 3M adhesive and press the mount firmly on the center console. According to the manual, for the best result, you should leave the mount on there for 24 hours before using it.

As shown in the product photo, the mount looks like a person sitting down with the adjustable mount as the person’s fedora. The mount comes with two metal discs where you can place one inside the phone case. Alternatively, if you don’t use phone case, you can use the 3M adhesive from the disc to place firmly on the back cover of your phone.

Overall, the mount is strong and can withstand various driving conditions. The current rating for this car mount supports phone with weight up to 88oz, but if you feel the need for an even stronger mount, be sure to check out VA-SH019, which supports phone up to 105oz in weight. Obviously, you need to take your phone case into consideration when making the right purchase decision.

I get this one because I do have a Moto E4, and the phone is so light weight that it doesn’t warrant a stronger mount that I use in my other vehicle.
label: positive

2.) The “stand” feature does not work with the new iPhone 14 Pro Max due to its weight. The phone is too top heavy and will fall backwards on the standard setting. I have to slide it to the absolute minimum setting in order to get it to free stand and even then it’s so unstable that you can literally blow it over with a short breath.

3.) This was mentioned in someone else’s review, I just want to hammer it home: it will stick to metal surfaces when you place your phone down and will detach from your phone when you pick it up. I honestly would save your money and look elsewhere for a different product, even if it’s a few dollars more.

text:
So I got it today and installed it in less than 1 hr...just followed a Youtube video on how to take the phone apart. The battery came with all the necessary tools. Separating the screen from the case was a little nerve-wracking but the plastic prying took along with the triangle tab was enough to get the job done. The video I wateched used a metallic shim to get the glass screen off, but I think the triangular plastic took was enough.

So far the battery charges fine. If the batter holds up after 6 months, I'll revise my rating to a 5...if not, then I'll downgrade to a 2 or 3. The iPhone 8 plus is a perfectly capable phone in my opinion, just seems a waste to upgrade unless there's some compelling reason to do so. This battery "upgrade" could be just just the answer if it holds up...time will tell.

**update 9/30/22**
It has been nearly 6 months and the batter still holds a nice charge. I can get through over a day of light internet browsing, heavy texting, and light youtubing without the battery draining. The Battery life indicator tells me it is still at 100% charge capacity…how accurate that is, I wonder. While the new battery certainly is much better than the used original…I do get the feeling it doesn’t hold the charge quite as well as it did 6 months ago. I don’t have any experimental or objective data…this is just going by “feel” based on past experiences, so it’s highly subjective.

Overall, I would say I am quite happy with this product. It definitely still holds a much better charge than the original and considering the price and relative ease in replacement…I would be fine replacing it a year from now if the battery starts dying again (assuming I don’t upgrade to the iPhone 15 by then).

I will keep the score at 4 because I don’t think 6 months is enough time to tell if this product will truly meet my expectations. Come April of 2023 if the battery still holds up, I will certainly update the rating at that time.

By the way, China is certainly in the midst of an economic contraction and will be in a deeper recession than us here in the States…not sure if this particular product will continue to be available in the next year…so if you’re looking to keep that iphone 8+ ticking for a while longer, I suppose now is as good as it gets.

title: Flimsy
text:
As far as doing what it is designed to do, it gets five stars. But it's too much of a distraction to a driver because of its flimsy construction.

The angle of the phone in the charger is controlled by a U-shaped piece of wire that lets one adjust the angle for best viewing of the phone.

The problem is that this wire is flimsy and doesn't "snap" into position. So every time the phone is jostled it collapses back onto itself, leaving the phone lying flat. Worse, because the wire is so thin it's difficult to pry back out with one's fingernail to reset to the proper angle. Especially while driving one-handed!

If this thing was designed to have some form of more rigid, durable, angle-setting anchor it'd get 5 stars. But as it stands it's a hazard to safe driving because it collapses the phone with some regularity during most of my trips.

Not recommended.

text: This is it -- THE most memorable of Hollywood's high-water action epics; yeah, I love "Captain Blood" and "The Adventures of Robin  Hood"; sure, there is nothing like "The Prisoner of Zenda"  (with Ronald Colman) for sheer derring-do and slapdash romantics but . . .  "Gunga Din" says and does it all -- with a broad touch of  screwball, bravado, wit, camaraderie, brashness, exuberance and downright  pleased as punch with itself fun; it's the only film I can watch beginning  to end, more delighted with each viewing and unbelieving that, after two  hours, there isn't more; and does it have anything to do with the Kipling  poem?  Some . . . but does that matter?  Not at all; this is a film about  the right stuff in British India during an 1880's resurgence of Thuggee  (the murderous Kali-worshipping stranglers that Indiana Jones had to  contend with in "The Temple of Doom"); Spielberg and Lucas owe a  lot to Stevens and "Gunga Din"; as does any director worth his  salt who wants to take a good shot at an action film that people will want  to sit through over and over.  Yeah, "Gunga Din" is broadly  acted, the action scenes are probably sped up, the black and white  photography gets a little grainy (someone please restore this movie! ), but  who cares -- the music, script, direction are sublime; the acting charming;  the end is something to get on your feet for. title: Great, if you don't have a leather backed LG G4.
text:
(To clarify, since Amazon has confusing review sorting/mixing: This is for [[ASIN:B00V2H4BSC Poetic's LG G4 Revolution Case]].)

First time ordering this, I wound up getting a screen protector in place of this case. Not sure how that happened, but, whatever, got a refund, ordered this again, a few days later, had the case for real this time.

It's actually a really solid case. It fits super tightly, which is to be expected. The built-in screen protector can turn out horribly bubbly unless you work on that for a little while, but besides that... It's just a strongly built case, I felt like I could throw it and not bring harm to the phone. Not that I'd ever do something like that. It feels great to hold, although I -was- accidentally touching the camera lens when trying to go for the power button, just because of how much "more" there is to hold. It's not that much of a weight addition, but it does feel way bulkier than the phone alone.

The reason I am giving this an average rating is because I actually have to send this back, because my LG G4 has a leather back, and I have no intentions of buying the different / "normal" back for the phone. Questions somewhere here on the amazon page ask if it fits the leather back, and most(all?) say it does. It totally does. But there's a major problem that comes up when you -do- have a leather back.

This case, specifically the piece that snaps onto the front of the phone, smothers the proximity sensor on my LG G4, and that causes the phone to refuse to unlock. The only way I could unlock my phone -- with the case on, anyway -- was by plugging it in for charging. Disappointing, because as I said above; I actually really like this case. Maybe it's my fault I went for the leather back. There's no way of manipulating the case or the phone, as far as I can see, to get this problem to go away.

Conclusion: Great, if you don't have a leather backed LG G4. I'm pretty sure you couldn't beat the price for what you get in return.
If you have the leather back, either buy the other back, or you'll come off of this disappointed in your decision to be Unique™.

P.S.
If you do purchase this case, be sure to have an empty pen or some kind of strong flat and thin object, as you'll bring pain to your fingers if you try to take the front piece out of the main piece otherwise.

title: Outright False Advertising - Not Ballistic Glass
text:
My first and major gripe with this product is that it is not as advertised. On the front of the box in big letters it says "GLASS" screen protector. Elsewhere on the box it says 9P hardness - an indicator of the strength of ballistic glass. Since I did a product search for ballistic glass screen protectors you'd think that's what you'd get. Right? Wrong!

I opened the box to see everything packaged nicely but was curious to see a squeegee to apply the protector. I've been using ballistic glass for about 3 years now and this is a new one to me. I took out a screen protector and it seemed rigid. No problem yet. However, the stiffness I noticed is only a result of the front and back backing/protecting plastic being firm. The first big problem is that on the side that touches the screen - the backing plastic is so tough to remove that it's not possible to do without getting a few fingerprints on the adhesive side.

This is also when I discovered that the protector is a soft TPE plastic not the ballistic glass the product makes you think it is. I read back through the description because it's possible I made a mistake. But no where in the description is it clear that this isn't glass. I figured, "What the heck" and gave it a try because it might be a good product. Because of the trouble with the backing plastic, it's almost impossible to apply the film without numerous bubbles. Once you've taken the effort and smoothed them all out it's time to take off the front protective plastic. Once again, the adhesive was so strong that it caused the screen protector to lift in many places and you had to go through the whole bubble removal again.

The real kicker though, is it didn't really stay attached over the curves. Even though the protector was close to perfectly positioned, the right edge lifted and wouldn't stay stuck no matter what I tried. The whole experience reminded me why I went to rigid glass protectors over 3 years ago. If you like this type of plastic film protector - the product may be good and may work well in your hands. But we were off to a bad start right away with the misinformation and the unclear product description.

title: You don't have to know who Magpul is to enjoy this case
text:
Regardless of what Magpul has in the rest of their product line, this case is awesome. I bought it for my new iPhone 5S recently as a backup case to my "business" Spigen case I carry at work. Case is very easy to put on (and take off) and fits like a glove. It is very tight when it is on and I have yet to see dust or debris make it behind the case....even after a three day trip fly fishing and carrying it places you shouldn't carry a new iPhone. Seriously, for under 20$, this is the best value for this style of phone case period.

Likes:

-Great fit and easy to take on and off...I don't feel like I'm "wearing it out" swapping it out.
-As everyone else has already said...it has a fantastic tactile feel that Magpul is famous for...good grip, but not too obtrusive
-I've had no problems with plugging head phones or chargers (Apple and aftermarket) into it and the camera cut out is fine
-Very good looking case...color options are pretty awesome as well.
-I haven't dropped my phone with this case on (yet) but I suspect it will protect the phone the same if not a bit better than other cases in the class

Cons:

-I don't care for the button covers. I get it...they keep out debris and dust real well. But I struggle with the volume buttons...especially when I'm trying to "snooze" my alarm in the morning. Maybe they will break in though...
-The "grid" design looks good and helps with grip...but I don't always enjoy holding the phone in the talking position with them. I almost wish I could get one that is just a solid case with their awesome coating.

title: Works well for Verizon 3G and  4G.
text:
Where I live i am bouncing between 3 bars 3g and 2 bars 4g service. My iphone 5 does not let me force it to stay in 4g so watching long videos is great if I can keep 4g but if it decides to drop to 3g the stream is interrupted an i have to start over :( I bought this item in the hope that it would boost the 4g signal enough to keep me in steady 4g coverage. It worked. when in the cradle my iphone 5 gets 2-4 bars 4g and holds it without dropping. I also used the cradle with my moms iphone 4 and it works well with it too (3g only)

speed test speed results:
3g no cradle: .4mb up .3mb down
4g no cradle: 7-12 mb down 3-5 mb up
3g with cradle (iphone 4 & 4s) .8-1 mb down and .8-1 mb up
4g with cradle 15-25 mb down 6-14 mb up.

I took a trip recently where there was only 3g coverage and the booster worked well for making a limited 3g signal steady and stronger.

The home kit [[ASIN:B003NQ5EWC Wilson Electronics Home/Office Accessory Kit for Wilson Sleek, C-Boost]] is well worth the price. The antenna mount is worth the piece by its self. I tried to make my own and had poor results. the desk stand is helpful but has a few issues (see issue two below). the home kit has a nice bag that fits the whole kit in one nice package.

I have had two issues with the cradle over the past 3 weeks. First, the side plastic things (hands) that hold the phone are not sized right for the thin iphone 5. it will work but the smallest plastic hands on the farthest in setting hold the phone but they bend in enough to make the outer 10% of the screen hard to touch. I have no case on my phone but using one should help this. I could also just cut the plastic tabs shorter. My moms iphone 4 in a hard case had no issues so bigger phones are fine.

Seconds issue is with the home mount kit. the attachment point for the cradle to the gimble base is loose and works well in vertical mode. put it into landscape mode off balance the whole thing and it tips over. the Iphone 5 is one of the lightest phones out there so bigger phones must have it worse. I can make it work most of the time by putting a book on the desk stand but its a design flaw. The weight needs to be hung more to the left if the cords for the power and antenna are going to come off the right.

2.17.13 update:
Still working great! I use it 8-24 hours a day and love it.

one note, it does get warm after long usage, it will make my Iphone5 very hot if I am say watching a video on the tv via steaming and using a lighting to HDMI adapter. It could be that the phone is getting hot and has no place to dump heat but the booster holder it is in. this is only a minor deal and I still enjoy this device.

3/1/2 update:
I tried using this cradle for two phones last night and it worked! Instead of putting the phone in flat I made a triangle out of the phones and cradle. and both iphone 5's got boosted 4g service! I uploaded a photo of the setup to the images of the device.

After receiving the watch (which took 2 days longer than originally planned) I charged it to full charge. Immediately had trouble connecting to the Samsung Wear app on my phone. After downloading several plug in updates it still did not connect. I finally got an answer on a blog I happened across. I basically had to go into the setting of the watch and select the option to add a new phone. Evidently it was still programmed to the previous owners device. Once it connected I enjoyed the feature rich options of the device. I explored many of the cool things it’s capable of. I did notice that after only about a half hour of use the battery was drained to 75%. By the time I went to bed it was 50%. I woke up the next morning and immediately checked the time on the new watch. The screen was black. I thought maybe it went dead during the night. My next thought was to check the app. I did and it revealed the watch was at 45% charge. Still the screen was black. Nothing I did made a difference. I put it back on the charger for the next couple hours. I would check it periodically To see if it would come on. Nothing. Finally while I was standing in the kitchen, I noticed it starting to blink and then.....boom it powered up! I thought great! Maybe it was a glitch or some kind of update it was processing. The excitement was short lived. With in 10 minutes of removing from charger the screen went black once more. This time never to show its face again ( no pun intended). At a hundred bucks I thought what do I have to lose. Surely they refurbished the watch and it should now perform good as new. Boy was I wrong. Maybe I got the lemon. Good thing is Amazon is great about taking stuff back so a thumbs up to them. Maybe next time I’ll cough up the extra dough to buy a new one. I would like to but simply can’t recommend. ******* Update: DO NOT BUY *******
I purchased a transparent one, as my old white one was getting dirty, and white one is no longer available. I received the transparent one, opened the box, and tried to put the case to my iPhone Xs, and the case self-destroyed, as in the picture. I did not put unreasonable force or anything. ******* Below was my original review *******
I have been using this product for about a week, and I am moderately happy so far. I used to use all-silicone transparent or white cases since my iPhone is always white and want my iPhone to look white even with the case. But the problem with silicone is, it easily takes color of jeans or other colored materials. For example, I have to throw away my transparent or white silicone cases typically after 2-3 months, since it got so dirty (blue most of the time).

I decided to try this case because the back of the case of hard (mimicking the back of iPhone Xs), and thus it doesn't (at least easily) take color, while the side bumper is silicone so the phone is protected by occasional dropping (I trust soft cases more than hard cases).

The quality looks good. The back of the case actually looks like iPhone (wish apple mark is there, but I guess it is impossible legally...) The case is very secure (indeed it is hard to take iPhone out of the case), and seems sturdy. So my first impression is good. We'll see how long it lasts (without turning blue).

One complain is that I wish the silicone is painted with silver-ish color so the side silicone bumper doesn't take color easily. But maybe since it is on the side, it might not take color easily. We'll see.

title: Good materials, with design flaws...
text:
The item is built pretty decent compared to others I've seen however there are some two critical design flaws.

1. There is a really long screw as you can see from the stock photos that are actually longer than it looks. It's used to put pressure on the CD slot to help hold it stable. The idea is good, but I found the screw to be longer than it really needs to be. Depending on your dash, this could get in the way of other dash function. On my Audi S4, it wasn't that big of an issue.

2. The biggest issue with it is the cup and ball design of the swivel where the mount connects to the device holder. I found that it doesn't allow you do tighten it down enough to get a really good secure fit. I had to undo it and put a couple layers of paper to give it some extra girth. Without it being tight enough, every time I went to rotate the holder, it would rotate at the cup and ball instead of the the part that should actually be rotating.

The screw that tightens the cup and ball is metal, but the part you handle to tighten it is plastic and I stripped it as I was tightening this down.

Overall, after I put the paper in it, I'm very happy with it. It's a clever idea to use the CD slot since no one ever buys CDs anymore. One thing I would watch out for is to make sure the phone isn't going to block what you need to get at.

text:
I've had three iPhones. A 3 a 4 and now the iPhone 5 (skipping the 3s and 4s). I've never felt compelled to write a review although I've liked each one. But the other day I dropped my iPhone into water, where it was submerged for several seconds. I thought it was a goner for sure. After drying it off there was still water seeping out from inside the phone. I did the old rice in-a-bag trick, which often works. My iPhone is back online, with absolutely no side effects from the submersion. This demonstration of quality compelled me to write a review for once.

On top of the many minor drops, sweaty runs, overuse, and general carelessness - the fact that it can recover from water submersion, to me, is a sign of a basic level of quality I need in a phone. Apple could probably manufacture these to fail under that level of mistreatment, so that we have to buy another, but they care about the performance of their product (in this case). So 5 stars for the iPhone 5.

Oh, by the way, the rest of the device is great too. Camera's nice, lighter than older models, quick LTE speeds, blah blah. Battery life is just acceptable, but not enough for me to dislike it.

text: This cable feels and looks well made.  The Lightning connector is very close to the original Apple size (measured with a caliper at 0.360" x 0.220") so I expect it to fit through any case.  The flat cable 0.18" wide by 0.08" thick and is very flexible.  It comes rolled up, and is quite compact.  I can't get it back that small, of course.  I'm not sure this is less kink/twist prone than other small round cables like the Frieq.  I have both, and don't have a strong preference either way, yet.  This has a slightly shorter strain relief and Lightning connector backshell than the Freiq, so it is a more compact configuration. It's 0.63" from the point where the metal Lightning "blade" enters the plastic backshell to the end of the strain relief, so if you have a situation where you need to get the cable to bend out of the way quickly, this is the cable for you.  As the cable is flat, it will tend to flex on that axis every time, while a round cable will distribute the flex and subsequent strain more evenly. Time may tell.

text:
This iPhone 6 case is an amazing wallet/case. The leather is as soft as an well oiled worn leather baseball glove and linings inside is reminiscent of a high priced men's wool jacket. Overall this case is 5+ stars. Highly recommend.

***90th day Review***

OK, so I've had this wallet case for around 90 days now and I thought I'd let you in on how well it's holding up. The leather wallet is still soft and visually appealing and I'm still getting compliments on it. However, the plastic case that holds the phone is extremely flimsy and has started chipping/breaking around the edges. Some of the breaks are very sharp and would be painful if you nicked yourself on one of the breaks. I've had to take the phone out of the plastic case and file down all the sharp edges. There is one very large split in the plastic that goes from the bottom to about the middle of the case. I have band-aided the crack with some fiber woven tape, but i'm not sure how long the tape will hold. My guess is maybe 6 mos. The last thing is that the wallet and plastic phone case have started to come unglued in the upper right corner. It's small but over time, unless I re-glue it, it will separate permanently.

For these issues, I am changing my review from 5 stars to 3 stars. The leather wallet gets 5 stars and the plastic case gets 1 star.

title: Sub-par phone for a low price
text:
Great phone with a great value for the price. The Moto G looks like a much more expensive phone, and the 3rd generation design clearly takes its inspiration from the latest iPhones. I am very pleased with the speed and responsiveness of the latest Android version as well. Migrating all my data from my previous phone was surprisingly easy.

Now for the bad part. There is a really horrible, unforgivable bug in the software version that comes pre-installed with this phone that will drive you insane. This phone CANNOT make phone calls or receive texts out of the box. Pretty horrible for a phone to not function as a phone. You would think that the geniuses at Motorola would have tested that first. Thankfully, a system update was all it took to fix the issue, but that bug cost me a day of phone service and hours of anger and confusion, as I thought it was an issue with my SIM card or my carrier. Apparently this is an issue with the firmware, so I will wave my middle finger straight at Motorola on this one.

Otherwise, the Moto G is a dream. It's everything I need it to be and the latest OS, Android 6, throws in a lot of nice-to-have bells and whistles. I think this is the best smart phone for your money on the market. Just wish they tested the damn firmware better.

UPDATE: After using this phone for a few months, I have run into a few serious hardware problems. I am now down-graded my review to 2 stars. After a few months, the self-facing "selfie" camera stopped working entirely. Recently my headphone jack broke. I can no longer play music through that jack. It's very annoying and I am going to try either repairing it myself or sending it back to the manufacturer. I can no longer recommend buying this phone after having so many problems in just a few months of normal use.

text: I have a friend who purchased this phone and recommended it, so I bought it with the idea I'd try it out for 30 days and return it if I just couldn't give up my iPhone. I was looking for a phone that was still 'smart' but more difficult to use to reduce my screen time. Well needless to say it was not returned -- I love it. It makes texting and using apps harder but nowhere near impossible -- just difficult enough to not do it mindlessly all day. There is also a desktop app I text from as well, so I just utilize that for any texts longer than a couple sentences etc. The battery life is awesome, especially when I compare it to my old iPhone. It will easily last all day, and it charges SO QUICKLY. I saw one reviewer below had issues with AT&T service -- I have AT&T and I haven't had a single issue. My unlimited data has always worked. My only initial issues were my running app would shut off after 5 minutes (this was due to a default setting I found and changed, all good now), and occasionally the Bluetooth can be spotty. The phone is so light, cute and runs quickly. I've had iPhones since they came out and this has been such a refreshing switch. For people looking to minimize phone use but still have a smart phone, this is the phone for you!!

title: This is probably the best screen protector I've found so far for the Galaxy ...
text:
This is probably the best screen protector I've found so far for the Galaxy S7, but it's a little tricky to get it just right. It's worth taking your time though.
Thanks to Samsung's stupid design to start curving the edge of the glass about a millimeter before the edge of the screen, it has been VERY difficult to find a screen protector that curves over the edges but still works with a case.
I found this screen protector CAN fit perfectly with the Galaxy S7 Spigen® [Neo Hybrid] Case, but it has to be aligned exactly right or some of the edges peel up a little bit in a couple of the corners. Here's what I did: I removed my case, thoroughly cleaned my screen (especially the edges, otherwise the screen will peel up over time). Then I put the case back on, being sure not to touch the screen. I then started to attach the screen protector, positioning it very carefully inside the edges of the case. Once the screen protector was on, it still had a bunch of bubbles, so I remove the case at that point, then pressed out the bubbles with the squeegee. Once the screen protector is attached, do not put the case back on for about 24 hours (this will help to keep the edges from raising). This is a somewhat lengthy process, but with mine, you can barely tell that there's a screen protector. Hope this helps some of you! :)

title: ... was my first iPhone 6 case and I really loved it. The only reason I'm rating it 3 ...
text: This was my first iPhone 6 case and I really loved it. The only reason I'm rating it 3 out of 5 is because the volume button sticked and for durability. For some reason the volume up clicked just fine but extra pressure was required to push volume down (a more important volume selection if you ask me!). It's not difficult at tall to install and it looks amazing. It even passed the "drop test" — I dropped my iPhone 6 and it held up. My phone was not damaged BUT the trim did get a bit scuffed. A day or two later I noticed that the band snapped where the silence switch is located. This happens to be the weakest spot on the  outer band and now it's pretty much useless. So I ordered the Spigen Neo Hybrid die cut aluminum case to replace this one and I'm VERY satisfied. This plastic one is great, but it won't last more than a drop or two. It will keep your phone safe but if you want something more durable, I would suggest the aluminum version. I dropped that one as well and the edge got a little scuffed and it bent the frame so I just took it off, bent it back (it wasn't too severe) and put it back together. It's in great shape and even though I dropped this one as well, it still holds up and I have full confidence that it's the best looking iPhone case that offers the best protection. Go with the die cast aluminum Neo Hybrid and you won't regret it!

title: Not as good as original Samsung battery
text:
I was worried at first that I wouldn't be able to get the case of my Samsung Tab-2 7 inch open without breaking something. The Youtube videos made it look lot easier. After 7 years, it was on there really good but I finally got it apart. Tools designed to open tablets and phones are highly recommended.

As other reviewers mentioned, all 6 screw holes didn't line up exactly with the ones inside the tablet so I had to carefully drill them out with a 1/16" drill bit. That being done, the battery was installed. I don't have a way to measure capacity, battery life, etc. but this replacement cell doesn't seem to have the same life as the original when it was new. Also, for what it's worth, the original battery weighed 2.7 ounces and this replacement 2.5. That may not translate to battery capacity, but it is a difference of about 8%. In the end, it was a cheap fix rather than having to trash my little Samsung.
